headline: Regional imaging and molecular profiles resolve structured Alzheimer's states and tissue-level changes
label: Cell Type Aware Disease Modeling
summary: New work pairs tissue-scale imaging with snRNA-seq and CSF proteomic geometry to resolve disease-relevant structure in Alzheimer's and ageing.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving disease-related structure by coupling molecular data to anatomically or topologically defined organization, with Alzheimer's disease as the main context. The HypoAD atlas combines MRI from 458 people with 614,403 snRNA-seq nuclei to map hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer's disease. A preprint applies diffusion geometry and persistent homology to ADNI CSF proteomics, identifying two dominant Alzheimer's states that differ in tau biomarkers. The corpus callosum work is methodological: it resamples the midsagittal structure onto a standardized grid for spatially detailed diffusion MRI, avoiding inter-subject misalignment. It is not molecular, but it reflects the same emphasis on standardized spatial frameworks. What is new is the pairing of imaging-derived structure with cell-type or state-level molecular resolution, though the items do not jointly integrate these layers.
